techniques.target: scan --writers over the ULA: only the plotter's own XOR reads figure pixels; only the guard painter changes attributes in play
guard records at 24962 + 8k (y, x, image, ink) from the plot callers
the XOR plotter 0xD52E kept; four 16 x 16 sprites per figure over the drawn image, chosen by return address (guards by IX)
Sinclair 48K ROM as alt ROM image 1, hooks at 0x386E
28 MHz inside each hook, the caller's NR 7 kept on the stack and put back

results.scope: 1 rzxarchive recording (6,241 frames, the first rooms); unit cases for the plot, the gun and the clear at four CPU speeds; 8 negatives; no hardware timing

pacing.coverage: Hook cost measured per plot in the simulator at 28 MHz over the recording; no JNext or hardware timing.
pacing.result: The hook adds about 14,800 T at 28 MHz a plot (about 3% of a 3.5 MHz frame) after the fast path; the game's own timing is unchanged otherwise.

dependencies.coverage: Every screen reader and attribute writer in the recording (scan, probes); 20 plotter call sites read statically, the guard, Sam and Monty callers reached.
dependencies.result: Only the plotter reads figure pixels (its own XOR) and only the guard painter writes attributes in play: the XOR stays, the painter is turned off.

feasibility.decision: Figures as sprites in the game's own colours over the kept XOR plotter, the guard painter off (the standing default).
feasibility.next_experiment: A longer recording reaching Monty, the gun and a caught guard: replay IDENTICAL with every negative control caught.
